clue.text: Got to love The Queen in the sack

indicators.note: in places the run of letters from love, The and Queen inside the word for the sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A lover is smitten with the Queen while in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got to' looks like part of a sentence about love, but it is the definition, as in 'it really got to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has got to you has upset or annoyed you, which is a synonym phrase for the answer.

clue.text: Have got to open cheese and cake

indicators.note: to open means the possession word cuts into the cheese

parts.note: brie is a French cheese
to own is to have got

explanation.surface: An order to cut into the cheese and the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square of chocolate sponge is the classic example of this cake.

clue.text: Swimmer red? Second bit of suit's split!

indicators.note: split says the word for red is broken open by the letter

parts.note: Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a left-wing red

indicators.note: second bit of picks the second letter of suit

explanation.surface: A swimmer turns red because their swimsuit has split.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish is a swimmer in crossword language, and this is one example.

clue.text: Cracking defaced finest china, I guess

indicators.note: Cracking says I breaks into the letters on either side of it
defaced removes the face, the first letter

parts.note: best means finest
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the value of fine china that is cracked and defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' takes B off BEST to leave EST. 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, meaning a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough guess at a quantity or value is a near synonym, noun or verb.

clue.text: Stops going topless and relaxes

indicators.note: going topless means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Someone stops going topless and calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax a grip is to loosen or slacken it, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Say yes to a cold pint after church

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation for pint behind the one for church

parts.note: C is the usual abbreviation for cold on taps
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a chilled pint once the church service is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to an offer is to receive it willingly, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Rascal that's withholding key ace of clubs?

indicators.note: withholding means the two words keep the musical key held within them

parts.note: a cad is a rascal
ie, id est, means that is
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A rogue is hiding a crucial playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace of clubs' suggests a card, but it is a golfer's helper who is expert with clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's assistant carries the clubs, so a punning expert with clubs describes them.

clue.text: Sure, go out with one sensitive to sexual stimulation!

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A cheerful 'sure, go out with someone' to a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing body zones that arouse desire when touched; the definition is the dictionary meaning.

clue.text: Spiky sort seen with diplomat in a cape

indicators.note: in places the diplomat inside the spiky word

parts.note: a thorn is something spiky
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A prickly character is seen with a diplomat wearing a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like clothing, but it is a headland: Cape Horn at the tip of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Horn is commonly called this, so it is an example of a headland.

clue.text: Like sex with Her Maj on E? In a way

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the letter E below the queen's letters

parts.note: as means like
it is slang for sex
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about the Queen and sex on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E' is the slang for ecstasy in the surface, but here it is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning so to speak or in some sense, synonymous idioms.

clue.text: Do not sit on top of surly dentists

indicators.note: on is used loosely here as a signal that the words before it are to be worked into a new order
top of picks the first letter of surly

explanation.surface: A warning sign in the waiting room of some grumpy dentists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a loose anagram signal, as in a show being put on in a new form; the surface makes it read as part of 'sit on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontist is an old, rare term for a tooth doctor, so the plural matches the plural in the clue.

clue.text: Party working with energy on your bike

parts.note: a do is a party
a machine that is on is working
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A party-goer pedals off full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away', as is the answer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rude British slang ways of telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Some cannot amend a memo for a pilot

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A note that some people are not allowed to change, sent to a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A NOTAM, a Notice to Airmen, is an official bulletin warning aircrew of hazards.

clue.text: Ignite row, having had fill of flak?

indicators.note: the word for row has been filled with the word for flak, which sits inside it

parts.note: a set-to is a row or fight
flak is anti-aircraft fire

explanation.surface: An argument flares up when someone has had enough of criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flak' reads as criticism, but here it is gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle something is to light it, the plain sense of the answer phrase.

clue.text: Get rate, say, to realign barn door?

indicators.note: to realign means these letters are lined up again in a different order

explanation.surface: A farmer asks for a quote to straighten a barn door.
explanation.walkthrough: A poor shot 'couldn't hit a barn door', so a barn door is the classic thing nobody misses.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is proverbially so large that anyone can hit it, an example of something impossible to miss.

clue.text: Terribly sore on my a— 'nuff said!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are mangled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a sore backside, then breaks off: enough said.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash cuts off a rude word, and the definition says why.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial ways of saying no further explanation is needed.

clue.text: Very hot broad, but not outwardly smart

indicators.note: not outwardly drops the outside letters of broad

parts.note: to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A sultry woman who is less clever than she looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad' looks like slang for a woman; it is just the word whose middle is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting day is a scorching one, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Shortly cuddle, but not with Penny

indicators.note: not with says the letter for penny is taken away

parts.note: to spoon is to cuddle

explanation.surface: A lover will soon cuddle, though not with someone called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in a little while, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What one might have with a large G&T?

definitions.text: What one might have with a large G&T?

parts.words: What one might have with a large G&T?
parts.note: a large gin and tonic promises fun; also, the answer phrase starts with G and the second word starts with T

explanation.surface: Asking what follows a big gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: The G and T are also the first letters of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fun night out is the natural result of strong drink, the cryptic picture.

clue.text: Painter shot by half-cut American

parts.note: a go is a shot or attempt

indicators.note: half-cut keeps just the first half of the word for American

parts.note: a Yank is an American

explanation.surface: A painter is shot by a drunk American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as tipsy, but it halves YANK to YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Give up the criminal life or turn and run?

parts.note: your go is your turn
to leg it is to run

explanation.surface: A crook ponders whether to go straight or flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg it' is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Going straight means becoming lawful, which is what the slang phrase means.

clue.text: Two favourites? Speed and heroin, son

parts.note: to race is to speed
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Two favourite things: amphetamine and heroin, a son confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' and 'heroin' suggest drugs; only heroin is one here.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is the runner most backed in a race, so two of them may well be thoroughbreds.

clue.text: After going all over the place, spy rare Banksy?

indicators.text: After going all over the place
indicators.note: the letters going all over the place are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: After roaming everywhere, someone sights an elusive Banksy.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is an anonymous British graffiti artist who works with spray paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy paints with aerosol cans, so he is an example of a graffiti artist using spray.

clue.text: Whitish lines yours truly snorted by notebook

indicators.note: snorted by means the pieces are drawn up into the notebook

parts.note: a pad is a notebook
L is short for line, so LL is lines
yours truly means me, the setter, I

explanation.surface: Someone pale has been snorting lines of cocaine off a notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale, colourless skin, whitish from illness, is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Folk are to put in new order, mind

indicators.note: put in new order plainly means the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange some people, mind you.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind children is to care for them, a synonym of the answer phrase.

clue.text: Port that shuts up at five to one?

indicators.note: that shuts up means the port's letters close around the other word

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port

explanation.surface: A port where everything closes at five to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five to one' looks like a time, but it is odds or a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Five to one expresses a proportion between two numbers, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Put off by cleaning product, chap leaves

indicators.note: leaves says the word for chap departs from the longer word

parts.note: detergent is a cleaning product
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A man is repelled by washing powder and walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to put them off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A recurrent idea? Tense man sat on Hoskins

indicators.note: sat on in a down clue puts the first pieces above the setter

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
he is a man
the setter Hoskins refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A tense man sitting on the setter has become a running gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif that keeps coming up in a work is its central subject, the synonym here.

clue.text: Pound to be put on Bud? Grrrrrrrr!

indicators.note: to be put on places the pound sign after the word for bud

parts.note: to bud is to grow
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A frustrated grunt about the cost of a Budweiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' looks like a beer or a friend, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The string of r's imitates a low rumbling snarl, an onomatopoeic stand-in.

clue.text: £100 returns on the cards — fat chance

indicators.note: returns means the slang for a hundred pounds is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred pounds
something on the cards is probable

explanation.surface: A gambler's hundred-pound bet on a card game has little hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sarcastic idioms for something that is never going to happen.

clue.text: Having pinched bottom, go now

indicators.note: having pinched means one word has nabbed the other and holds it inside

parts.note: a go is a try
the bottom is the end

explanation.surface: After pinching someone's backside, it's time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now' is the definition in its slang sense of fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Now' as an adjective means of the current moment and fashionable, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Warning: outspoken nude is … gran?

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the word for nude is said aloud

parts.note: bare means nude

explanation.surface: A warning that a naked figure is in fact a grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gran?' with a question mark marks an example: a grandmother is one kind of ancestor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is anyone you descend from, and a grandmother is an example.
